subject: SIG: audit log slices, customer export access, and retention evidence
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@greenfin.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@greenfin.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: SIG follow-up: audit log slices & third-party SIEM exports

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for walking us through the SIG last week. A couple of follow-ups from our security team regarding audit logs before we close the item:

1) Can you confirm whether customers can request an export of a specific time slice (e.g., a week) of raw event logs for ingestion into our SIEM? If so, what formats and retention windows are supported?

2) We need an example export (schema + a 24-hour sample with anonymized data) to validate parsing rules.

3) For the retention evidence: can you provide the policy document and a recent retention summary that shows when events older than X days are purged? Our requirement: retention audit trail for at least 365 days with proof of deletions for older slices.

4) Finally, does Redwoods provide a read-only API key or delegated access model so our SOC team can pull slices directly into our SIEM (Logiq) without a manual ticket each time? If there are rate limits or SLOs you impose, please call those out.

Appreciate a short plan and ETA. If useful, loop in your security engineer.

Best,
Alice
Director, Security Engineering
GreenFin Capital

--
Note: this message contains project-specific requests tied to our SIG questionnaire (section: Audit & Logging).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@greenfin.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: audit log slices & third-party SIEM exports

Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Evelyn (Security) and Monica (Customer Success) to scope the sample and walk through options. Quick answers up front:

- Yes, customers can request time-sliced exports of event logs. Supported formats: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) and compressed CSV.
- Default retention is 365 days for full fidelity event logs; aggregated indices are kept longer. We can provide retention policy docs and deletion confirmations.
- We support a delegated, read-only API token scope for log export; there are rate limits we can tune per enterprise customer.

Evelyn — can you confirm attachments we'll provide and whether the team prefers the sample as ndjson or CSV? Monica — please propose an ETA for delivery and coordinate any necessary DocuSign or data transfer approvals.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@greenfin.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T08:24:18-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: audit log slices & third-party SIEM exports

On Mon, Nov 15, 2026 at 9:12 AM Alice Chen <alice.chen@greenfin.com> wrote:
> Thanks for walking us through the SIG last week...

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. Short plan and deliverables below:

Deliverables we will upload to the shared Drive by EOB 2026-11-18:
- Redacted 24-hour sample (ndjson) of API + system event logs (filename: audit_log_schema_v2.csv and audit_log_sample_20261114.ndjson in the Drive).
- Retention policy excerpt (redwood-retention-policy-2026.pdf) and a retention-summary CSV showing job run timestamps for purges over the last 18 months.
- Export playbook (log-export-playbook.pdf): steps to request an export, how to request a delegated read-only token, and rate limit guidance.

Technical notes:
- Export formats: ndjson (preferred for SIEM parsing) and gzip-compressed CSV. Fields included: timestamp (RFC3339), tenant_id, request_id, user_id (anonymized for shared samples), event_type, resource, status_code, latency_ms, src_ip (anonymized), agent_string, and raw_payload (when permitted).
- Delegated access: we support a scoped API token with read:logs permission. Tokens are auditable and rotate on manual or policy-driven schedules.
- Retention enforcement: retention jobs are run nightly; deletion events are written to a "retention_audit" ledger which includes job_id, target_date_cutoff, rows_deleted, and checksum of deletion manifest. We can export that ledger slice as proof.

Open question for GreenFin: do you prefer token-based direct pulls or an SFTP drop integrated with your SIEM ingest connectors? We can enable either.

I'll attach the schema and playbook in my next message (sensitive fields redacted).

Evelyn
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: audit log slices & third-party SIEM exports

Hi Alice / Logiq team —

Following up to share the final sample and a short checklist for integrating with your SIEM:

- We have placed audit_log_sample_20261114.ndjson (anonymized) in the Drive link Monica shared. The file includes 24 hours of normalized events with tenant_id mapped to an opaque GUID.
- For token-based pulls: endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/logs/export?slice_start=2026-11-14T00:00:00Z&slice_end=2026-11-15T00:00:00Z ; scope: read:logs:exports. Rate limit: 2 concurrent exports per tenant; typical export throughput: ~200MB/min depending on compression.
- Retention proof: See retention-manifest-2026-11.pdf in Drive. The retention_audit ledger can be exported per-request; we included a sample manifest that shows job_id, run_ts, target_cutoff, and rows_deleted hashes.

If GreenFin approves token-based access, we will:
1) Provision a scoped token and send it to your security mailbox via encrypted email.
2) Run a one-hour parse test with Logiq to confirm mapping fields.
3) Harden S3 transfer permissions if SFTP is chosen.

Alice — please confirm preferred ingest method and whether you need a signed copy of the retention manifest for your audit. Once we have that, we can close the SIG item and mark evidence delivered.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
